title: Antiquated
body:
Goodbye Google Keep. It was kinda good while it lasted. You were my one and only, my go-to note app, my ride-or-die. But after years together, you simply have not evolved. There's a world of excitement out there and I'm ready to explore. "Why?" you ask? I'll try help you understand...at first, you labeled/tagged my inner most thoughts and it was so cool.  But when I needed to BOLDLY emphasize, you were nowhere to be found. Also, your fonts are restrictive and boring. I kept hoping one day we could get fancy together and dress up our notes. I've grown tired of the same ol' wallpaper...a fork? a pencil? Seriously? They gave me the icks! Oh yeah...and I always had to search through each separate Gmail account to find what I wanted. If only we could've searched all those accounts in one fell swoop. But noooooo. Sorry. I should've known better than to expect a surprise of new features and options. Was that too much of an ask? Everyone else has fancy things to look forward to. Me? I'm too restricted and bored with this relationship. We've been together for years, but it's time for me to set myself free! After all, it's true; the features are greener on the other side. 
Goodbye Keep🫥

title: Terrible Photo/image/ScanLacking layout.
body:
CRITICAL UX/ACCESSIBILITY DEFECT: Broken Document Flow and Layout Regressions in PDF Generation
Google Keep is currently experiencing a severe, unacceptable design failure regarding media handling that completely breaks user workflows and document accessibility. Forcing all attached images into a rigid gallery cluster at the absolute top of a note destroys data integrity for chronological procedures, tutorials, and step-by-step guides.
Severe Operational Bottlenecks:
 Broken Flow / Layout Degradation: Forcing text to separate entirely from associated media is a massive regression compared to standard industry tools like Apple Notes. It disrupts technical workflows and renders sequential notes useless.
 Systemic Print Failure: Exporting or printing to PDF strips all chronological context, rendering the output completely broken and illegible for operational use. Text → Image → Text interleaving is fundamentally required.
 Accessibility / UI Defect: Grouping all structural media at the top prevents logical screen reading and standard reading comprehension patterns.

title: Frustrating Experience on IOS
body:
I really want to like Google Keep because the concept is great, but using it on iOS has been incredibly frustrating. The biggest issue is the keyboard behavior. Whenever I’m editing a note, if I stop typing for about 5 seconds, the keyboard drops down and disappears on its own. I then have to tap the screen again just to bring it back up, which completely breaks my flow.

The same thing happens when I’m creating a list. If I hit enter to start a new line and pause for even a moment, the keyboard vanishes again. This happens constantly and makes something as simple as writing notes or lists way more difficult than it should be.

For a note-taking app, this is a major usability problem. Notes should be quick and effortless to edit, not an exercise in fighting the interface. Until this keyboard issue is fixed on iOS, Google Keep is honestly more frustrating than helpful.

title: One fatal flaw destroys accessibility
body:
It’s great to have it sync with family and Google Home.

But my primary use case is shared lists, and Keep has horrible accessibility.

On iOS, there is a three second timeout after which keyboard focus leaves a list item, finalizing the list item with whatever text was input. If you are a slow typer or use alternate input means - or even if you just need a few seconds to form your thoughts - google keep interrupts you.

You end up with empty list items because you didn’t type fast enough. You end up making multiple list items instead of one. You end up cut off with half written list items.

Unless you are a fast typer who always has fully formed thoughts ready to input without pause, this app is nearly unusable.

This no doubt demonstrates the limitations of a formulaic user testing process. I have a hunch that the Keep QA team has list entry items ready to go, and quickly runs through tests, rather than testing real world use cases - especially with a variety of accessibility considerations.

title: Missing important features to make it a daily notes app
body:
Google Keep is missing tons of features to make it highly useful notes app. When you look at what’s missing compared to the majority of notes app, it’s just a sticky notepad that can link to Google services.

•Rich Text Formatting – Bold, italics, underline, strikethrough, bullet points, checklists, tables, and more.

•Nested Folders & Subfolders

•Document Scanning

•Password Protection & End-to-End Encryption

•Rich Media Embeds / attachments – inline images, sketches, PDFs, and even web links with previews.

•Collapsible Headings

•Deep integration with OS and other devices

title: Amazing App! But could be better!
body:
I’ve used Google Notes since I’ve had a phone and it’s been a while. One thing I’ve noticed; It’s dependable, it’s clean, the UI is easy to use, and the added features are nice! HOWEVER, it would be nice if they could these 4 new features!
1. We can upload our own background to our notes. The default backgrounds they have are nice but very reminiscent of early 2000’s. It could be nice to either add some more variety or just let users have the option of adding their own. 
2. Adding music to notes. I like listening to classical music when I write and study and having multiple devices set up doing a million things at once all at one desk can get pretty overwhelming fast. But having my iPad play classical music while I’m using Notes to study? Way easier. Whether it’s Spotify or YT or Apple Music, or even just default sounds like rain or piano noises, something to listen to. 
3. A widget. Everyone else in the reviews would like a widget. And I’m a sucker for herd mentality. Plus I need one more to fit in my Home Screen. 
4. Visual organization of the notes itself. You can either sort your notes by boring rectangles of the same shape or varying squares. Some of my notes are long and some are, like many other users, short to-do lists, I’d like to be able to format my notes in a more aesthetically pleasing manner. Also, keeping with aesthetic, it’s either dark mode or light mode. If we could either change the background on that or be granted the option of changing how we read the notes, like in library apps. 
Overall, this app is really good. But it could be better.

title: Missing important features
body:
I came here to get away from Evernote because it was so bad at syncing, but this is worse. 

- You cannot add a list to a note with regular text — it will convert the entire note to list form. 
- Once you have converted a note to a list (whether by accident or not)) you cannot undo it.
- You cannot copy an entire list. You can only copy one line item at a time.
- There is no way to view the date of when your note was created, only the last time you edited it. So if you accidentally click in to the note, you now have no idea when you created it.

title: Easy to use, feels unfinished.
body:
Wanted to write a review because since downloading this, I've been using it constantly, but there are some missing QOL type features it could really use.

I'm not entirely sure who the target audience is for this app, and I don't think Google does either. They should probably pinpoint that so they can make the app feel more focused. Right now, it feels kind of like a digital "refridgerator door" that you can throw tons of colored sticky notes and photos on, mostly intended to be used as to-do or shopping lists.

Despite the vague design, it works really well for MY purposes. I write lots of stories as well as draw, and I'm pretty ADHD-brained. Because of that, all the other apps I've tried to take notes on left me frustrated due to being cluttered with too many bells and whistles, user-unfriendly interface, or just not having a type tool at all. Ideas can come to me any moment so I love being able to whip out Google Keep, quickly type out the idea and add it to the rest of my notes. The sheer simplicity and ease is what I like about it, I really don't need much. However I think the app can still be improved without losing this simplicity.

There is one main feature I REALLY REALLY WANT that I am suprised is not already built in. My favorite thing about the app is being able to organize my notes with labels (as well as colors). I give my all my notes 2-3 labels or so, so I think it would be logical to want to narrow down my search with MULTIPLE labels. It would make sorting things much more intuitive especially at the rate I'm adding new notes. There are a few other small annoyances caused by missing features, but this one is by far what I want to see in the app the most.

Please keep updating and improving this app! It has been so great at helping me get pen to paper. There is a lot of potential but Keep isn't there yet.

- Frequent lagging to register typing, so I start retyping and then my previously typed letters suddenly appear

- Switching between different notes within the app is EXTREMELY laggy, to the point I’m frequently unsure if my tap on the note even registered and if it will open. I’m talking like 10-15 second lags.

title: Dreadful
body:
I’ve used the native Apple Notes for years without a problem, and it did everything I needed. I even tried several other apps a few years ago to see if something would be better for me, but nope, I was satisfied. 

Then Notes started crashing. Someone suggested Google Keep but wow! Look at the problems! Some people sneer at Notes, but their problems are nothing like this! Even the issues the most helpful reviewer Geo_ has are crazy because if my notes aren’t organized, what is the point? I’m going through Notes, stashing them in places, deleting them as I go, hoping I find the corrupted file that makes my Notes crash. I'm only using this when I have to when a file's format is incompatible with another stop-gap measure or if I want to save something quickly. 

This is a poor excuse for storage. I don’t want to fling information into a repository- I want Folders. Inside the folders, I want related files, and I want to do that on the fly. Apple Notes allows me to create Folders and "notes" that function as 2nd level storage. I can rename files as I go. Keep barely recognizes "labels" until I’ve started filling them.

• What's with the miserly colors. What’s the point? There are 14 combined colors & patterns, but I can’t add my own. 

• Markdown. Seriously? Is it so complicated to incorporate Markdown? I rely on formatting, but it’s whisked off when it hits Keep. Is the Metadata still there? I doubt it.

title: Doesn’t print in full screen, crashes, annotations on pictures loses item
body:
I have been using this for 10 years. It’s a great place to take pictures/screenshots and organize. But some warnings: 
*when printing, it prints out 1/4 the image size. I take photos of my kids school art. When I tried to reprint, it only printed 1/4 the size, making it useless 
*it doesn’t sync with google photos nor google drive 
*when taking a photo and annotating or drawing on the photo (i.e., writing on the photo or drawing an arrow), the app crashes and the photo is now blank (as if the app is trying to resync but never does), so the item is lost 
*too many options photos on a particular keep note, the app will crash when trying to open the photo
*app doesn’t always sync between devices or takes forever.
 I have three devices and don’t see the image across my other devices, so sometimes have to type in the notes vs relying on images 

 The pros: *if using only the text, sharing a list with friends is easy *i still use the app but with the warnings above *no space/size limitations and its free *using on both android and ios (note the caveat above on images) *a good way to save stuff (i have a “note” for kids school art, take photos of my monthly bills, articles from magazines, etc)

title: A glitch no one’s been talking about ruined my experience.
body:
I’ve been using this app for years. But around two months, I started running into a huge problem every now and then. I’d be in the middle of working on a note when randomly I’d be booted out, and left to watch from the menu as all my notes mass duplicate themselves and turn into lists. This also affected my archived notes. The original versions of the notes would copy paste all text three or four times, enter checkbox format, then make two other blank versions of it also full of checkboxes. In the middle of cleaning up my page (this is the third time this has happened, though it’s never been this bad.) one of my most important notes went missing out of nowhere. I found it in my trash and when I went to restore it, it came back blank.

This app has had an irreplaceable role in not just organizing my goals and daily life, but my enjoyment of poems and songwriting. Until I can be for certain my hard work will be protected, I’ll be forced to use a different notes application. I hope this issue gets resolved because it hasn’t been a one-time occurrence. Each time it has gotten worse. Each time I’ve lost valuable information. Each time I spend hours of my day having to clean up and rewrite notes that were altered by a bug that seems very recent.

I hope this gets resolved so that I may return.

title: Why do Google apps like Keep have third-rate search?
body:
Keep could be an essential note-collection tool: it’s intuitive, simple, fast and offers valuable features like extracting text from almost any image saved to a Keep note.

What relegates Keep to a 3.5 star afterthought is its weaknesses in something Google arguably does better than anyone on Earth: search. 

Perhaps there’s some super-strategy behind Google’s decision to make searching in most of its non-Gmail products worse than what we were able to accomplish in a 1980s DOS command. But the fundamental purpose of collecting notes in an app is to have key information available when we need it later.

I’ll concede that Keep does allow searching by content type, labels and the text within notes. But certainly Google (whose name is universally used as shorthand for searching) has the technical chops to include advanced search in Keep and all their products.

Where is:
 ›› Find notes created in a date range, or modified, or before?
 ›› Search for duplicate (or similar) notes?
 ›› Advanced search operators (AND, OR, NOT)?
 ›› Multiple search criteria, and saved searched?

None of these missing key features are blue-sky next-gen technology. They’re the foundation of what Google does, and users deserve tools with at least the capabilities of 1980s-era software.

title: Trash
body: Buggy. Idiosyncratic. Drawings don’t scroll without inexplicably zooming. Free movement of canvas/drawing area is limited. Not enough white space provided to do math problems without bumping against an immovable border. Document spontaneously closes when merely drawing a line from left to right with the stylus. Document reopens NOT at the level of the last edit but all the way at the very top, forcing endless scrolling just to get back to your work, at which point you draw a left-right line and it closes again. Typical poorly implemented, inconsiderate Google garbage. Time-wasting. Effort-wasting. Makes no sense. Designed by half-awake, out-of-touch engineers looking for a paycheck. Bad UI. Bad UX. Maybe good for you if you need a gimmicky one-trick pony with an absurdly narrow range of functionality.

title: Decent so far, but only a B+ rating
body: This is my first time using Keep for iOS, and I'm impressed thus far. However, I have 3 moderate gripes to share: 1) I wish the app would retain the label selection when reopening the app. For example, if I have my "Things to Do" label filtered and then close the app, I would like for the "Things to Do" label filter to still be enabled when I relaunch the app. It wipes the label filter every time and displays all notes again without a filter. This gets annoying to reselect each time. 2) A nice enhancement would be to auto-invite collaborators to any notes within a specific label. Currently, I have to invite my partner to every note one-by-one. This gets somewhat tiresome after 30+ new note invites, which also spammed her email inbox with 30+ notifications. That workflow could be improved. 3) If inviting a collaborator to a note, have the assigned label(s) carry over to the collaborator's Keep. For example, I assigned my partner to several "Gift Idea" labeled notes, but she had to go in and manually create/assign the same label within her account so that we maintained the same label. These labels should sync across, in my opinion.

title: Good app, just some suggestions
body:
GOOD FEATURES
1. The labels feature and options to change the background color of each note is helpful for organization 
2. It’s cool you can add drawings, voice recordings, images, reminders, and checklists. And the feature that grabs text from an image was very useful.
3. Of course the ability to share notes across devices and between people since notes are saved with your Google account and not just downloaded to your device.
4. Small thing but being able to copy stuff to Google Docs was nice
5. Aesthetically pleasing. Not that important but if an app looks old I’ll be less likely to choose it

IMPROVEMENT SUGGESTIONS
1. Add bold, italic, underline, and text size
2. Make the option for images to be embedded at any place in the note instead of just attached at the top
3. Allow checkboxes in between paragraphs instead of requiring the whole note to be a checklist 
4. Add a view option where only the note titles are shown (instead of the larger icons; like the list view in Google Drive)
5. Allow multiple reminders in one note (not as important as the other ones)
6. Automatically change links into their image previews, while still leaving the option to remove it. Usually I prefer the link icon over the long chunks of text.

title: The good and the bad
body:
—Update 3/15/2020—
It looks like they have fixed the default account problem listed below. I added a star as a result. If someone at Google is reading these reviews – thank you! Now please commit to real release notes listing the fixes and changes of each release instead of the generic, “Bug fixes and performance improvements.” The good news is it appears they are looking to continue to improve the product instead of letting it die like some other Google products.

—Original 12/1/2019—
As a teacher I love Google Keep for keeping track of things I see or read to clip and save for later. Whether it’s a site that might be useful to my students or an image for a future lesson, I can easily Keep things and even sort them by topics. So far so good, but there’s one “feature” that has killed me over and over. When I choose to Keep something I have to manually select the Google account I want to use even though I only use Keep with one account. There is no way to even set a default account to be used for new notes. There is no way to disable Keep for an account. As a result, every time I Keep something I have to first choose the correct account before I can submit it. It takes what should be a very quick process and turns it into a multi step process. Things sometimes get put under the incorrect account when I’m in a hurry and then I have to go find a note that’s missing. Losing things in an app designed to keep things organized is less than ideal. It’s such an easy fix, but it remains a problem. Minor fixes getting ignored makes me worried about Google’s plan to keep Keep.

title: A few UX opportunities
body:
Overall this is a fine app for notes and checklists especially when considering the benefits of it being slotted into the Google ecosystem.

However there are two UX issues that come to mind that stop me from being all that happy with it.

The first is a lack of a platform standard left edge swipe gesture to return to the top level list view from an individual note. You’re relying on users to tap the upper left arrow. Not conforming to basic platform conventions makes this app stick out as being inconsistent. There must be another way to make a checklist item a “sub” item — it’s frustrating to constantly do this on accident.

The second issue I see is the floating of the “add” and “more” icons at the bottom of the display when the keyboard is open. Users assume that toolbars floating above the keyboard relate to the task of typing. e.g. in the stock iOS notes app, quick actions to adjust type formatting. Instead, these icons have more to do with the overall note. The ... “more” icon would probably make more sense in the upper right next to archive. The add button might make more sense as a floating action button in the lower right, visible when the keys are hidden.

author: JrewAM

title: The Lack of Dark Mode is Unacceptable (A Rant Review)
body:
I want to say first off that Google Keep is fantastic and is what I take all of my notes in. I use it every day and so should you.

The reason I’m giving the iPad app one star is because of a lack of a dark mode, and there are a few reasons for that. First off I want to say that I have never even considered giving an app 1-star for a lack of dark mode before now, and I think in most all cases it would be a dumb thing to do.

HOWEVER! As a cross-platform focused app that I use on my Android, my desktop, my laptop and my iPad it is extremely frustrating that the iOS version of the app is the ONLY version that does not have a dark mode. Android and Web both have it and it’s fantastic. 

I find it extremely frustrating when a company the size of google can’t deliver what I and many others consider an accessibility feature to a platform as big as iOS, especially when iOS has Dark Mode built in and is pushing devs to implement it in their apps, AND when Google has just added Dark Mode as a native feature to Android, which shows that they DO care about it and they DO know that it’s a big deal.

That’s why the lack of a dark mode is so unacceptable, and I stand by my reasoning for it. But what really drove me to write a review and give 1-star (other than it being the best thing I can do to try to get Google to hear me) is a situation that arose last night.

I was going to bed and decided that tonight was the night that I prepare for the ideas that pop into my head while I try to fall asleep. I use Keep religiously for this, because it helps to much to get a thought out of my head and into the app so that I can focus on sleeping instead. But I always do it on my phone, which often leads to me doing other things on my phone afterwords because one thing leads to another and it’s so comfy browsing my phone in bed. I want to stop this, but when I try to control myself and not pick up my phone my thoughts that I’d write down just keep me awake. And I can’t use pen/paper because I like the room pitch black while I sleep.

So I decided that I was going to put my iPad on my nightstand, hooked into it’s keyboard and with Keep loaded up so that when I have to jot something down I can just reach over, tap a key twice, and I’m ready to go. Simple, streamlined, and a lot harder for me to get distracted and start browsing other things. It’s a perfect solution.

So I set it up and open Keep, and then I remember about the lack of Dark Mode. I look through settings and they still haven’t implemented it. So I stare at this horribly white screen and realize that I can’t use it, so I open up the native iOS Notes app instead and use that.

That’s why I felt compelled to give this 1-star. The lack of a basic accessibility feature that the app has on every other platform made it so I was better off using a different app, and while Notes is fantastic nowadays, it’s not cross-platform.

So that was my long-winded, “first-world problems” 1-star review of my favorite note taking app. I love it and that’s why I care so much.

To anybody reading this: Please use Google Keep, because it’s amazing.

To Google: Guys....plz

A useful concept, a free version of Evernote that integrates well with other Google apps?!

No. That's not this app. Keep is a light weight toy that's more like iOS Notes. However Notes performs, Keep will literally lock your whole phone for nearly a full 20 seconds before processing a command. 

That's because, I'll admit, I love to keep digital artifacts. I keep articles, job postings, shopping links, all to come back to and inform a new decision. I work in marketing and it's useful to have great copy or designs to reference.

Keep can't keep up, simply can't hang. It offers one of the poorest user experiences out there and I think that's simply because it was never built to do what I think most people would love it to do: keep stuff. Keep is useful if you just want to jott something down quick and delete it soon after. I actually enjoy pen and paper for that! 

Wish me luck, I'm about to clean out my sluggish Keep app and move over to Evernote.

body:
So Google makes a big deal that Keep’s latest feature is it works on the Apple Watch. Sounds good, right? But in true Google fashion, no-one appears to have actually tested this. 

IMHO the primary use case for this functionality is to take notes when your phone is not available. Which means network is likely not available. And what happens when you take Keep notes on your watch and the network is not available? 
Oh, it looks good, they appear on the watch just fine. Until network becomes available; at which point they are deleted!

So... an app whose sole function is to take notes, yet which cannot reliably retain those notes? Not sure quite what the market for that is.

There are rarely to never new features and it seems clear that the Keep platform is in stasis, soon to be replaced with whatever bright and shiny thing Google chases next. Too bad, because Evernote is a slimy company and I can’t bring myself to use OneNote. And Bear’s web app will never be released; they’ve been promising it for two years and it’s not in beta yet. 

Keep’s style of note taking and web clipping is unique and fits me the best, plus it integrates with G-Suite. It should be the center of my workflow, but instead it’s the product I have to use because there’s simply no good alternative. 

I fully expect it to look and function exactly the same in a year.

~~~~~~~~~
9/17: I love the interface and idea behind google keep, and the online version is fantastic, but the iOS app is pretty much the most frustrating thing in the entire world for me, All because the lag time is completely insane.

When I open the app, it takes a good 15 seconds for everything to ‘update’ so that I can start tapping around or scrolling through my lists or anything.

If I just keep typing away, it will take about five or six seconds, and then all of the letters I’ve been typing will pop up really fast but then it will pause again and do it all over. It is so godamn frustrating, all I want to do is type like normal, like every single other app will let me do. 

My phone is relatively new, my operating system is up to date, and this problem has been going on with Google Keep on iOS for the entire year I’ve had my phone since I switched over from android. I reeeeeeally need to give it up and just switch to Evernote. 😡😡😡

title: Used to love this app
body:
I used to love this app. My wife and I kept a shared grocery list as well as others. The grocery list, by far, gets the most use.  For the last year and a half, it has become pretty buggy for me. Lists would disappear, updates made by one collaborator would not show up for the others on the list. Now, lately, I can’t seem to add an item to my grocery list without the app crashing. I’ve closed the app on my iPhone, restarted it, shut the app down, hard booted my phone, created a copy of a list and deleted the original to see if one was corrupted, you name it, I’ve tried it.  Now, not only does the app crash most of the time, when I do successfully add a line item, instead of keeping it where I added it, Keep tosses the line item down to the bottom of the list.  I’m not able to move the item in the list order now as well. I’ve taken great pains to order the grocery list to coincide with the layout of my local grocery store.  It’s WAY more efficient that way. Now it’s becoming an aggravation.  I’ve got over 300 items in my list. Starting over would be a headache. I’m not really interested in using one of the other shopping apps that force a subscription or demand an account be set up for all members to share. I really liked the way Google Keep used to work. Google!  Please fix this app!!
For what it’s worth, I’m using an iPhone 6+ with iOS 11.3.whatever the latest is.

title: Incredible productivity tool!
body:
This app has quickly become one of my go to apps throughout each and every day.

It’s cross-platform approach makes jotting a note on my phone, revising it on my Chromebook, then converting it to a Google Doc on my desktop a snap. It is lightweight in terms of storage space and processor demands, yet it is robust in its abilities. Saving audio, photos, etc into notes is simple. Setting reminders, even recurring reminders, makes this app outrageously useful for jotting quick reminders when adding something to a calendar is just too time consuming. And again, the cross-platform approach means that the reminder pops up on your iPhone, your Chromebook, and your Windows machine (or Mac) unlike Apple’s native reminder / to do apps. Of course, you have to be using Chrome on your computers as the internet browser. But why wouldn’t you? :-)

In all, it’s a very useful app for organizing and staying on top of personal and professional business!

title: Lag, non-responsive, failures to sync
body:
I am hugely reliant on this app. Unfortunately, since iOS 11, and especially with this most recent app update, the app has become very unstable. 
Syncing across my devices is sketchy at best, and information disappears. I’ve had to recreate whole sections of notes which sync my updates; rather, the app took the updated note and synced it backwards to the previous version on another device. 
Response to touch / type /cursor movement is slow at best, but usually impossible. You can’t move the cursor anywhere. To move in a note, you actually have to exit the note, re-enter it, carefully place the cursor at what you need to edit (nowhere else!), then exit again, and re-enter it at the next place to edit. Any attempt to move the cursor or tap elsewhere in the note has absolutely no response. 
I hope this is rapidly addressed, as otherwise Keep is a lifeline app for me.

title: Zero crashes on my iPhone 7 Plus
body:
I relunctantly installed Keep after reading the negative reviews regarding crashes. But I was on a quest to find a way to keep my thoughts, plans, interests, and things I find on the web that I'll need later (I hate browser bookmarks.) And the solution must be cross platform (i.e. Work on anything.)

After a month of using Keep it has won me over. No bugs or crashes. 

AND there is a Chromebook app for Keep. And it works exactly like the mobile app but just a bigger display. Since it's updated in realtime it doesn't matter when I make an entry it always shows up on every device and computer I own.

Android, Windows and Mac support exist as well, of course.

Further, you can add collaborators to Keep entries and this makes it very nice to be able to share things with my wife. The grocery list, Christmas list for our son, etc

I'm hooked.

For those who try Keep and don't like it, check out Dropbox Paper. It just came out - still in beta as I type this.  It would have been my next choice if Keep didn't work out.

I have a never ending battle between using Google or Dropbox. Google won out in this area. 

It's a great time to be alive. Twenty years ago this technology would have seemed like something out of a Star Trek movie.

title: Useful service, glitchy app
body:
I've used Google Keep for years, and it's remained one of my favourite Google services to date.  I hoped it would function as cleanly on iOS as it did on Android.  

Instead there is a major functionality bug.  When using Keep in another app that has a scrolling feed (such as Twitter or Tumblr), specifically using its pop-up view to save a link to Keep, it freezes the scrolling feed of the other app, making it impossible to interact with.  

The only way to "unfreeze" it that I've found is to hit another button on the nav bar of the app.  So in Twitter, if your home feed freezes, hit the icon for messages or search or whatever to "unfreeze" the app, making it function as normal.  (Try it for yourself - "share" a Tweet link via Keep, save it, and watch what happens to the Twitter app).  

But if you're in an app (or a section of the app) with no access to the nav bar, your app will freeze totally and you will have to force close and restart it.  This is obnoxious and frustrating if you're just trying to use an app in peace.

Two, currently, it only allows one level of items.  It would be nice to have multilevel items.

Three, Google keep and Google calendar integration.  It is desired to have Google keep checklist items with a due date to appear in Google calendar.

For now, I am using Microsoft outlook and Wunderlist to achieve the above.  Since Google is ignoring Google tasks, I suggest Google to add more features to Keep so that Keep can replace Tasks.

title: Fixed my crashing Keep app!
body: Update-this bug which causes Keep to continually close is content specific. It was only a problem on one of my Google accounts and not the other. I resolved it by logging into Google Keep from Chrome on a laptop. Next I went to settings and disabled "display rich link previews". I then went through each note and deleted the URL previews that had been automatically added. Finally I deleted the app from my phone and re-installed it. After a few minutes all my notes re-sync'd and that app didn't crash anymore!

title: Almost there...but "almost" relates it to useless
body:
Google Keep is great app...almost.

First, Google Keep's best features:
     - The very direct checklist UI. Easy to reorder, fast to check off, clear indication of completed items either inline, at bottom of the list, or hidden
     - The excellent use of both iPad and iPhone screens, using 3 columns on the iPad and 2 on the iPhone. Most apps waste the screen real estate by using only one column.

There are three limitations however that unfortunately relegate Google Keep to the "maybe someday" pile of my unused apps.
     1. The max box size renders lists near useless. You have to open a list to see if what you are looking for is further down the list. GK needs to let lists grow endlessly
     2. The manipulation of lists only by opening the list. It would be much faster and more direct to simply check items off or reorder them directly in overview panel 
     3. The "forcing" of a horizontal layout or boxes, rather than allowing a vertical layout. A vertical layout option would offer more better harmony between the 3-column iPad and the 2-column iPhone.

title: Another weak iPhone app from Google

Also, if I use 3D touch to save an audio note, why does the share to an e-mail app include only the (often poorly rendered) voice-to-text translation and not the actual voice message?  Puzzling.  

I would actually pay for good Google apps.  Come on, Google.  Well, at least Google Calender is a good app.

title: A good app, but syncing is broken
body:
If you make a list, then edit the list on a device without service (which shows the old version) once that device gets service, it syncs the outdated version to all devices.

I was in the grocery store trying to load my shopping list I made on my computer at home. I had an old version of the list loaded on my phone. When I moved to a spot with service, the old version I was looking at suddenly saved over the list I made on my computer at home.

Similarly, making changes without service also is broken. If you make changes without service, then get service, it saves over your changes with the last saved version.

It's a pretty gaping hole that makes the app unusable. I'd love to use the app, because it is great, but I can't.
